newsitem.title: USA: Construction spending unexpectedly strong in September.
newsitem.headline: Construction spending unexpectedly strong in September.

text.p: The biggest jump in government-financed building projects in more than 5-1/2 years during September gave the construction industry an unexpected boost, the Commerce Department said Monday.

Total spending on new public and privately financed construction climbed 1.9 percent to a record seasonally adjusted annual rate of $573.4 billion -- the biggest increase since a 2.3 percent gain last March and sharply contrary to Wall Street economists' forecast of a 0.1 percent decline.
Both privately financed and public, or taxpayer-paid projects, increased in September, but by far the largest part of the increase was in government spending.
Government spending shot up 6.4 percent in September to a rate of $147 billion after a 1.4 percent fall in August.
There were big rises in spending to improve highways and streets and smaller increases for housing and redevelopment, schools and hospitals and for water treatment plants.
On the private construction side, overall spending edged up 0.4 percent to $426.4 billion after a 1.4 percent increase in August.

Spending on single-family homebuilding fell to $155.9 billion in September from $157.3 billion in August. But there was a significant increase in spending on non-residential buildings to a rate of $142.3 billion from $140.3 billion in August.

After allowing for inflation, total construction spending rose 1.7 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted $496.3 billion annual rate following a 0.5 percent rise in August, the department said.
